answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted identity with a sunk cost. An agent must lock scarce capital before it can earn, and peer ratings make its work a costly signal, since a fraudulent identity forfeits the whole bond on discovery. Forgery does not scale by copying software. A sybil farmer must fund a separate bond for every puppet, and those bonds can be slashed together, so attacker cost grows linearly while influence stays flat. The honest network is a trellis: each reputation claim rests on verified bonds below it, and no fake branch grafts onto a real vine without paying full price.
